fullPassage:
Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain.

(C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress.

(A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.

(B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

questions.passage: Stress not only ①<u>affects</u> physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, ②<u>made</u> us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something ③<u>stressful</u>. One study ④<u>demonstrated</u> a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② made → making: 분사구문으로 주절 보충 설명. 'Stress affects... , making us...'에서 현재분사 making이 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① affects: 주어 Stress(3인칭 단수)에 맞는 동사
❌ ② made: 분사구문에서 능동의 의미이므로 making이 적절 ←정답
✅ ③ stressful: something + 형용사 (후치수식)
✅ ④ demonstrated: 과거 시제 동사, 주어 One study에 적합
det.tip: 분사구문: 주어가 능동이면 V-ing(현재분사), 수동이면 V-ed(과거분사). Stress makes us → making us

det.korean: ③ monitoring → to monitor: 'helps you to monitor'에서 help + 목적어 + to부정사 구문. help는 to부정사 또는 원형부정사를 취한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① remain: help + 목적어 + 동사원형/to부정사 (remain resilient)

❌ ③ monitoring: helps you to monitor가 원문 — 동명사 monitoring은 부적절 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ what → which: 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 관계대명사 which가 적절. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 부적합.

✅ ③ resilient(회복탄력적): 원문 일치
✅ ④ confuse(혼란시키다): 원문 일치
det.tip: reveal(밝히다) ↔ conceal(숨기다). studies done to reveal = 밝히기 위한 연구
